title: Sunny and the Night Flowers | Bedtime Story
description: Sunny the quokka discovers flowers that only open when the stars come out, and watches the bush fill with its own secret moonlit garden. A soothing story from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories, perfect for little ones drifting off to sleep.
narration:
The afternoon had been long and warm, and now the sun was going down, painting the sky in soft pinks and oranges. Little Sunny the quokka was wandering through a quiet corner of the bush she had never visited before.

That was when she noticed them.

Tucked low between the pale rocks and the silver grasses were small round shapes, tightly curled like tiny closed hands. They were flowers, Sunny could see — but they were not open yet. She sat down very quietly to wait.

The sky deepened to soft purple. The first star appeared, small and still. And then something very gentle began to happen.

One of the flowers — a soft white flannel flower — began to unfurl. Very slowly. Its petals opened the way a yawn opens, all at once and quietly, as if it had simply been waiting for exactly the right moment.

Then another opened. Then another.

One by one, all through the clearing and along the rocky edges of the path, the white flowers opened in the moonlight. They were soft and round and still, and they seemed to glow with their own gentle light, each one a small bright face turned up toward the stars.

Sunny turned slowly in a circle, looking all around her. The whole bush had its own secret nighttime garden — and she had never known it was there.

She lay down among the blooms. Their petals barely touched her fur. The night air was cool and sweet. The flowers were still. The stars were still. And Sunny was still too.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, night flowers. Goodnight, little one.
